New: Why Should We Care if the Illicit Iran-China Oil Trade Goes Through Malaysia?

Roughly $4 billion a month. That is what Iran’s sanctioned oil trade with China was worth when it ran normally, according to Charlie Brown @supbrow, and the revenue goes directly to the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps.

Brown, a former U.S. Navy officer who heads the Iran Tanker Tracking Program at United Against a Nuclear Iran, joins @GordianKnotRay and Jim Carouso from Singapore to explain how Iranian crude reaches China’s teapot refineries by way of an anchorage 80 nautical miles from Singapore, often relabeled “Malaysian blended crude.”

He calls Malaysia’s Eastern Outer Port Limits “parking on the side of a superhighway.” The location is within Malaysia’s Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), shallow enough to anchor and close enough to Singapore for resupply. Ships go there, he says, “precisely because they won’t be disrupted.” None anchor in Indonesian waters, where Jakarta’s enforcement is stronger across its full maritime zone, having once seized the Iranian-flagged Arman 114.

Malaysian fines run just five figures against cargoes worth $100 million, which Charlie calls a slap on the wrist. This past January, Malaysian authorities detained two false-flagged tankers conducting a transfer off Penang, then released them with a minimal fine, which changed nothing at the Johor anchorage. Malaysia updated its EEZ Act in June 2026 to cover illegal anchoring and unpermitted cargo transfers across its maritime zone, but Brown says nothing has really changed.

Also in this episode: what the U.S. blockade has and has not stopped, why 26 Iranian-flagged tankers sailed within days of the MoU signing, and Brown’s argument that roughly a third of these ships are now stateless and can be seized by any nation on the high seas.

There is a class of people in this world who benefit from division. Not just racial division—any division. Race, ethnicity, religion, region, language, tribe. It does not matter what the line is, as long as it keeps the working class from uniting around the only question that actually threatens them: who owns the resources?

This class is the transnational capitalist oligarchy. They do not care about Black, Indian, white, Sunni, Shia, liberal, conservative, or any other category. They care about the rate of profit. And the most efficient way to protect that profit is to ensure that the working class never unites against them.

The mechanism is the comprador duopoly. Two political parties. Two ethnic constituencies. Two elites. Both tied to foreign capital. Both incapable of breaking with imperialism. Both competing to see who can best serve the empire while keeping the working class from rising up. The people are told to choose between “our turn” and “their turn.” They are never offered the best option of a united working class as the ruling class, and benefitting from their own resources.

Trinidad and Tobago is now being subjected to the same playbook that destroyed Guyana in the 1950s and 1960s. This is not speculation. It is just history repeating itself.

The Guyana Precedent: A Multi-Ethnic Movement Destroyed by Design

In the 1950s, Cheddi Jagan built the People’s Progressive Party in British Guiana. It was a multi-ethnic, working-class movement. Indian and African workers organized together. It was a genuine threat to the colonial order because it united the two largest ethnic groups against the British planters and the American corporations.

Jagan wanted to nationalize the bauxite and sugar industries. The bauxite was controlled by Alcan and Reynolds Metals—American corporations. The sugar was controlled by Booker McConnell—a British corporation. Nationalization would have transferred those resources from foreign shareholders to the Guyanese people.

The CIA and MI6 did not send in troops. They did something smarter and more cynical. They fractured the movement along racial lines. They pushed Forbes Burnham, an Afro-Guyanese politician, to split from Jagan, an Indo-Guyanese politician. They funded Burnham’s campaigns. They planted stories in the press. They made each group afraid of the other.

Then they let the violence do the rest.

The result was a descent into manufactured racial violence that devastated the country. In the mining town of Wismar, Afro-Guyanese mobs, with police standing by, drove the entire Indian population of three thousand from their homes in an orgy of arson, beatings, and rape, forcing them to flee across the river to Mackenzie. Across the colony, arson became a daily occurrence. Indian and African families who had lived as neighbors for generations turned on each other with cutlasses and fire. Nearly two hundred people were murdered, over a thousand were injured, and more than fifteen thousand were forced from their homes before the December 1964 elections. The British colonial authorities, who had spent years cultivating the division, stood aside and let it burn.

The socialist project died in the ashes. Burnham took over and ruled as a corrupt, authoritarian figure who kept the foreign corporations happy. The bauxite stayed in foreign hands. The sugar stayed in foreign hands. The working class—both Black and Indian—got nothing. The elites rotated. The foreigners kept extracting.

Guyana never fully recovered from this betrayal. It is a warning that every Caribbean nation should have learned by heart.

Why the US Wants Control of Venezuela and Trinidad

The Energy Prize

Trinidad and Tobago is not a minor player in the global energy market. It is Latin America’s largest LNG exporter and the second largest in the Western Hemisphere after the United States. In 2025, it shipped over 10 billion cubic meters of liquefied natural gas—roughly 2 to 3 percent of global LNG trade.

But the volume is not what matters. The ownership is what matters.

The Atlantic LNG facility, the country’s sole export terminal, is 90 percent owned by foreign corporations. Shell owns 45 percent. BP owns 45 percent. The Trinidadian state, through the National Gas Company, owns just 10 percent.

So when T&T ships gas to Europe—and it shipped over 3 billion cubic meters there in 2025, a market that grew dramatically after the destruction of Nord Stream—the profits do not stay in Port of Spain. They flow to London. And they flow at a premium: T&T’s LNG cargoes have been sold at prices 15 to 55 percent above the US Henry Hub benchmark. That premium is pure surplus value, extracted from Trinidadian gas fields and transferred to British shareholders.

Venezuela sits on the world’s largest proven oil reserves—over 300 billion barrels—and significant natural gas reserves. The US wants control of those resources. The kidnapping of Maduro in January 2026 was not about democracy or drug trafficking. It was about oil. As Trump openly stated: “We’re going to have our very large United States oil companies... go in, spend billions of dollars, fix the badly broken infrastructure, the oil infrastructure, and start making money.”

The 2027 Convergence: Supply Shock Meets Strategic Timing

Every major project in the Trinidad-Venezuela gas corridor is targeting first gas in 2027. This is not a coincidence. It is a convergence engineered to maximize profit from a global supply crisis that is already underway.

The International Energy Agency has warned that global LNG markets will remain tight through the end of 2027, with a cumulative shortfall of roughly 120 billion cubic meters between 2026 and 2030. The cause is the US-Israel war on Iran and the resulting disruption of the Strait of Hormuz, through which nearly 20% of global LNG supply transits. Qatar’s export capacity has been cut by 17%, with repairs expected to take three to five years.  Future disruptions may be far worse if fighting escalates again.

Into this gap, the Trinidad-Venezuela corridor is set to deliver:

- BP’s Ginger field (Trinidad): first gas in 2027 for liquefaction at Atlantic LNG. Peak capacity of 62,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.

- Shell’s Manatee field (Trinidad): first gas targeted for Q4 2027, with the pipeline capacity from Venezuela increased from 700 million to one billion cubic feet per day.

- Shell’s Aphrodite field (Trinidad): first gas anticipated by Q2 2027, following commercial agreements finalized in September 2026.

- Shell’s Dragon field (Venezuela): a four-well drilling campaign begins Q2 2027, pending a final investment decision. The field holds an estimated 4.2 trillion cubic feet of gas. Roughly 70% of the gas is destined for Atlantic LNG, with the remaining 30% for the petrochemical sector.

- Shell’s Loran-Manatee field (cross-border Venezuela-Trinidad): first gas targeted for 2027. Loran holds 7.3 trillion cubic feet and Manatee an estimated 2.7 TCF.

- EOG’s Coconut project (Trinidad): first gas expected in Q3 2027, adding 300 billion cubic feet to the domestic supply network.

The timing is the point. The US and its corporate partners have spent years preparing the legal, financial, and military architecture to control this gas. The destruction of Nord Stream, the sanctions on Russia, and the war on Iran have created the tightest LNG market in decades. And the first gas from the Trinidad-Venezuela corridor is set to flow precisely when the global supply gap is widest and the premiums are highest.

This is the petro-gas-dollar in operation: the deliberate destruction of competitors’ export capacity, followed by the precise timing of alternative supply under US political control. The working class of Trinidad and Venezuela does not own the gas. It does not own the infrastructure. It will not receive the premiums. It will receive wages, and it will receive a racial or national grievance to distract it from the fact that the wealth is leaving.

The Mechanism of Control: OFAC Licenses

The entire mechanism of US control over this energy corridor rests on the sanctions regime against Venezuela’s state-owned oil company, PDVSA. Because of these sanctions, any company—including US allies like Shell or BP—that wants to do business with PDVSA or develop Venezuelan energy resources requires a specific authorization, known as an OFAC license. This gives the US government a legal chokepoint to control all such economic activity.

The US uses this power to grant, deny, or revoke licenses, directly controlling whether projects proceed.

- The Dragon Gas Field: T&T was first granted a license for the Dragon field in January 2023. This license was later revoked in April 2025 by the Trump administration, effectively halting the project.

- The Manakin-Cocuina Field: A similar pattern occurred here. BP had an OFAC license, but it was revoked in 2025, stalling development.

This shows that even when a project is technically feasible and has Venezuelan approval, it cannot proceed without continuous US permission. The licenses are often short-term, creating uncertainty. For instance, the renewed license for the Dragon field was granted for only a six-month period.

The most potent part of the mechanism is the financial condition attached to the licenses. New licenses issued to BP and Shell in February 2026 require that any payments of royalties and Venezuelan taxes go through the U.S.-controlled “Foreign Government Deposit Fund”. This effectively means the US Treasury acts as the banker for the project. Venezuela does not receive its revenue directly. This accomplishes two goals simultaneously: it strangles Venezuela’s gas revenue, and it directs the project’s output to US-aligned markets.

The gas itself is processed in Trinidad, specifically at the Atlantic LNG facility and the Point Lisas industrial estate. The plan is for Venezuelan gas to be liquefied at Atlantic LNG and exported to global markets, particularly Europe. The pipeline route involves connecting Venezuelan gas fields directly to Trinidadian infrastructure—from the Dragon field via a subsea pipeline to Shell’s Hibiscus platform, and from the Loran field through the Shell-owned Manatee platform in Trinidadian waters.

Military Integration and the Donroe Doctrine

The “Donroe Doctrine” is the Trump administration’s modernized, aggressive interpretation of the Monroe Doctrine, asserting the Western Hemisphere as a US strategic sphere and “limit[ing] the influence of rival powers” like China, Russia, and Iran. In this framework, the Caribbean is not a collection of sovereign nations but a “backyard” to be disciplined.

Trinidad and Tobago’s integration into this architecture has been rapid and comprehensive.

Within months of taking office, the UNC government shifted Trinidad from a “left-leaning stance centered on non-interference” to a “security-based alliance with the United States under the framework of the ‘Donroe Doctrine’”. This was formalized on March 7, 2026, when Trinidad joined the Americas Counter-Cartel Coalition (ACCC) and signed the Doral Charter, pledging military and intelligence cooperation.

The concrete results followed immediately:

- The US installed an AN/TPS-80 G/ATOR radar system in Tobago—a sophisticated air and missile defense radar that analysts explicitly stated “can be used in US conflict with Venezuela,” located just 70 miles from Venezuela’s coast.

- Trinidad opened its airports to US military transit and hosted US Marines for extended training exercises.

- The government joined the US Southern Command’s Joint Task Force, integrating its Defence Force into a US-led command structure.

- The State of Emergency, declared in December 2024 and extended multiple times, provided the domestic legal framework for this integration. It allowed for detention without charge, which was used to muzzle opposition to the government’s pro-US shift. The US provided a list of “persons of interest” linked to drugs, firearms, and violent crime—meaning US agencies were directly identifying targets for detention within T&T’s domestic security apparatus.

The Elite Rotation: Why the UNC Replaced the PNM

The shift from the PNM to the UNC is not a story of ethnic replacement for its own sake. It is a story of elite rotation in service of a geopolitical realignment. The Indian-led UNC offered the Western empire something the Black-led PNM refused to give: unconditional integration into the US military and energy architecture of the Caribbean.

The PNM under Keith Rowley maintained a foreign policy of non-interference and regionalist sovereignty. Rowley explicitly rejected the idea that Trinidad should take instructions from the US Embassy. The PNM pursued the Dragon gas field with Venezuela on its own terms, securing a 30-year license in December 2023 under the Biden administration. This was a project of national energy security, developed in partnership with Caracas and the European major Shell, not as a lever for US geopolitical pressure.

Most importantly, the PNM refused to fully integrate Trinidad into the US military apparatus. Rowley warned that Trinidad would become a “soft target” in any US action against Venezuela. The PNM’s stance was that Trinidad’s interests lay in regional peace and sovereignty, not in becoming a forward operating base for the empire.

The UNC under Kamla Persad-Bissessar offered the US everything the PNM withheld. Within months, Trinidad joined the ACCC, signed the Doral Charter, accepted the installation of the G/ATOR radar, opened its airports to US military transit, and integrated its Defence Force into US Southern Command. The UNC abandoned the PNM's 30-year Dragon license and accepted a six-month OFAC license in its place. The brief timescale was not an accident. As the Trinidad and Tobago Newsday noted, the six-month timeframe "heaps pressure on this country to keep its foreign policy aligned with American interests". And this realignment was enforced through a years-long State of Emergency that saw thousands of people including opposition figures detained without charge or trial, effectively silencing domestic dissent as the government dismantled Trinidad's sovereignty piece by piece.

The Indian elite that the UNC represents does not own the LNG. Shell and BP own 45% each. The Trinidadian state owns 10%. The Indian elite is a comprador class. It profits not from national development but from integration into the US-controlled energy supply chain. The US wants Venezuelan gas processed in Trinidad for Western markets. The UNC delivers that. The PNM’s insistence on a sovereign, long-term deal with Venezuela was an obstacle. The UNC removed it.

The Universal Mechanism: Beyond Trinidad and Tobago

The Structure of the Duopoly

The Trinidad case is not unique. It is the latest iteration of a mechanism that has been applied across the Global South. The structure is always the same:

1. Limit the choices: two comprador parties, both tied to foreign capital, both incapable of breaking with imperialism.

2. Assign ethnic constituencies: each party claims to represent one ethnic group. Each promises “our turn” in the state apparatus. Neither promises to change the ownership of the means of production.

3. Let them rotate: when the people tire of one, they vote for the other. The new party purges the old party’s appointees. The new elite takes over the state apparatus. The contracts are redistributed. The profits still flow out.

4. Inflame divisions: every rotation is accompanied by a crisis—a plot, a scandal, an assassination charge, a state of emergency. The crisis justifies the purge and disciplines the losing faction. The working class is told that the problem is the other ethnic group, not the class that owns the country.

5. Suppress the alternative: any party that threatens to break the duopoly—a genuine working-class party, a socialist movement, a multi-ethnic coalition—is crushed. The CIA does not need to send troops. It only needs to fund the factions and let the violence do the rest.

The Examples

Guyana: Cheddi Jagan’s multi-ethnic PPP was destroyed by CIA/MI6. Forbes Burnham was installed as a comprador. The bauxite and sugar stayed in foreign hands. The working class got nothing.

Fiji: A duopoly of indigenous Fijian and Indo-Fijian parties, with military coups serving as the rotation mechanism. The real issue—land ownership and resource control—is never addressed.

Malaysia: A duopoly of UMNO and opposition parties, with ethnic quotas serving as a distraction from class. The Chinese and Indian minorities are played against the Malay majority, while the real wealth remains in the hands of a small comprador elite.

Rwanda: The Belgians constructed Hutu and Tutsi as distinct ethnic categories, then played them against each other. The result was genocide. The mechanism of division reached its logical endpoint.

Sri Lanka: A duopoly of Sinhalese and Tamil parties, with civil war as the endpoint. The working class was destroyed by ethnic conflict while the elites rotated.

Kenya: A duopoly of Kikuyu and Luo parties, with ethnic violence as the electoral mechanism. The land question—who owns the country—is never addressed.

The Class Logic

The comprador elite profits from integration into imperialist supply chains. The foreign owners extract the surplus. The working class gets wages and a racial grievance.

The empire fears class consciousness more than it fears any military. Because if the working class ever united around the question of who actually owns the country, the whole system would be exposed. The foreign shareholders would be named. The local compradors would be exposed. The entire extraction racket would collapse.

That is why the empire spends millions to cultivate ethnic grievances. That is why it funds the parties. That is why it plants stories in the press. That is why it uses the CIA to fracture movements. The goal is not to have one ethnic group on top. The goal is to ensure that no class consciousness ever emerges.

Conclusion: The Choice Between Division and Solidarity

Do not fall for the “our turn” narrative. Do not look at a purge and think that justice is being served. Look at it for what it is: a distraction.

The real question is not which ethnic group controls the state apparatus. The real question is which class owns the resources. And the answer in Trinidad and Tobago is the same as it was in Guyana: not us. It is Shell and BP. It is the transnational oligarchy. It is the empire.

The only way to change that answer is to unite across ethnic lines. Not as Black workers. Not as Indian workers. But as workers—as the class that produces the wealth and receives nothing in return.

The foreign owners know this. That is why they spend millions to keep us divided.

The Same Mechanism in the Imperial Core

This is not just a Caribbean story. The duopoly is not a Caribbean invention. It is the general form of bourgeois rule in the modern era, and it operates wherever the working class must be prevented from uniting around the question of who owns the resources.

The United States is the most advanced case. There, the duopoly is not organized primarily around ethnicity. It is organized around culture. But the mechanism is identical.

Two parties. Two constituencies. Two elites. Both funded by the same donors. Both committed to the same foreign policy. Both incapable of challenging the ownership of the means of production. The working class is told to choose between red and blue, between “traditional values” and “progress,” between the party of the ownership class or the *other* party of the ownership class. It is never told that the real question is which class controls the government and owns the country.

Race still functions as a division—a powerful one, deliberately cultivated. But culture is the primary weapon in the American duopoly. Abortion, guns, gender, immigration, religion, flags, sports, entertainment, language. Every issue is engineered to sort the working class into two camps that hate each other more than they hate the class that owns them. Every election is a referendum on the culture war, not on the distribution of wealth. Every four years, the losing side is told to fear the winners, and the winners are told to despise the losers. And while they fight, the billionaires extract.

The mechanism is the same as in Trinidad. The parties rotate. The elites rotate. The policy stays the same. The wars continue. The wages stagnate. The debt grows. The infrastructure crumbles. The planet burns. And the working class is told that the problem is the other half of the working class.

The Same Trap, the Same Choice

The duopoly in the United States, the duopoly in Trinidad, the duopoly in Guyana, the duopoly in Fiji, Malaysia, Rwanda, Sri Lanka, Kenya—they are all the same structure. They are all designed to prevent the working class from asking the only question that matters: “who owns the resources?”

The answer in the United States is the same as the answer in Trinidad. Not us. It is the billionaires. It is the transnational oligarchy. It is the empire.

The choice is not between red and blue. The choice is not between Black and Indian. The choice is not between “our turn” and “their turn.”

text:
Guys, ada satu pertanyaan yang menurut gue paling penting dan paling relevan untuk Indonesia di 2026 ini.

Apakah kita sedang menuju Reformasi Jilid 2?
Dan sebelum dijawab gue mau jelasin dulu kenapa pertanyaan ini bukan lebay. 
Bukan lebay karena orang-orang yang mengajukannya bukan mahasiswa yang emosional. 

Tapi Mahfud MD mantan Ketua MK dan Menko Polhukam. Komisioner Komnas HAM. 
Pengacara senior yang berpraktik di pengadilan setiap hari. 
Dan aktivis 1998 yang pernah menggulingkan Soeharto dengan tangan kosong.

Mereka semua berkumpul di satu forum di Yogyakarta. 
Dan mereka semua sampai pada satu kesimpulan yang sama:

Sesuatu yang sangat serius sedang terjadi.
Dan ini perbandingan yang paling penting kondisi sebelum 1998 vs kondisi sekarang:

Sebelum 1998:
Rupiah dari Rp2.500 anjlok ke Rp16.000 dalam hitungan bulan. 
PHK massal. 
Harga kebutuhan pokok naik tiga sampai empat kali lipat dalam seminggu. 

Rakyat antre panjang di depan toko yang kosong. 
Kepercayaan kepada Soeharto yang sudah 32 tahun berkuasa habis dalam semalam.

Sekarang 2026:
Rupiah sudah di Rp17.700 dan diprediksi bisa ke Rp22.000. IHSG ambruk ke level terendah sejak COVID minus 22% dalam satu tahun berjalan. 68% pengusaha tidak akan rekrut karyawan satu tahun ke depan. 

50% tidak akan ekspansi lima tahun ke depan. 
Kelas menengah menyusut dari 57 juta ke 46 juta dalam satu tahun. 
Daya beli terus tergerus.

Belum separah 1998. 
Tapi arahnya sama. 
Dan yang paling mengkhawatirkan Mahfud MD bilang kita sudah masuk ke tahap kedua dari skema keruntuhannya:

Distrust → Disobedience → Disintegration.
Distrust sudah terjadi sejak lama. 
Disobedience pembangkangan terbuka terhadap hukum dan otoritas sudah mulai muncul di mana-mana.

"Apa yang bisa mengendalikan kehidupan kita sebagai bangsa kalau hukum sudah tidak bisa lagi mengatur atau menjamin ketertiban kita di dalam hidup bernegara?"

Dan ini tiga syarat yang membuat Reformasi 1998 berhasil dan mana yang sudah terpenuhi di 2026:

Syarat pertama: Krisis ekonomi yang tidak bisa lagi disangkal.

Di 1998 — krisis ini memuncak dalam hitungan bulan. Sangat cepat dan sangat brutal sehingga tidak ada narasi apapun yang bisa menutupinya.

Di 2026 — krisisnya ada. Tapi lebih lambat dan lebih tersembunyi di balik data BPS yang memakai standar garis kemiskinan yang terlalu rendah, dan klaim pertumbuhan 5,61% yang sebagian besar ditopang belanja pemerintah dari defisit.

Tapi rakyat merasakannya. 
Setiap hari. 
Di warung yang mulai sepi. 
Di PHK yang terus terjadi. Di dompet yang makin tipis.

Syarat ini: setengah terpenuhi. 
Krisisnya ada tapi belum sampai titik yang membuat semua orang tidak bisa lagi mengingkarinya.

Syarat kedua: Gerakan yang terorganisir dengan agenda yang jelas.

Di 1998 — mahasiswa dari berbagai kampus menyatukan diri dengan satu tuntutan yang sangat sederhana: Soeharto turun. 

Tidak ada agenda yang lebih rumit dari itu. Dan kesederhanaan itu yang membuat gerakan bisa menyatukan jutaan orang dari berbagai latar belakang.

Di 2026 — ada keresahan yang sangat luas. 
Ada demonstrasi. Ada gerakan Indonesia Gelap yang sempat menggerakkan ribuan orang. 

Ada Peringatan Darurat di 2025 yang membuktikan bahwa satu postingan media sosial bisa menggerakkan massa dalam hitungan jam.

Tapi belum ada satu tuntutan yang cukup sederhana dan cukup kuat untuk menyatukan semua keresahan itu menjadi satu gerakan yang kohesif.

Rocky Gerung menyebutnya dengan sangat tepat: "Kita marah ke segala arah. 
Artinya marah tanpa arah."

Dan Oki — aktivis muda mengakui: "Saya tidak lagi berpikir soal menurunkan Prabowo Gibran. Tapi saya berpikir paling tidak di pemilu mendatang kita tidak akan jatuh ke lubang yang sama."

Ini adalah strategi jangka panjang. 
Bukan revolusi. Tapi konsolidasi.

Syarat ini: belum terpenuhi. Keresahannya ada tapi organisasinya belum.

Syarat ketiga: Elite yang memilih untuk tidak bertahan bersama kekuasaan yang sedang runtuh.

Di 1998 — momen paling menentukan bukan ketika mahasiswa menduduki DPR. Tapi ketika para pendukung Soeharto mulai satu per satu meninggalkannya. Ketika menteri-menterinya mengundurkan diri. 

Ketika Harmoko Ketua DPR meminta Soeharto mundur. Ketika Wiranto tidak memberikan perintah tembak kepada tentara yang sudah dikepung demonstran.

Di 2026 — AHY dari dalam kabinet sudah mulai bicara tentang ego sektoral yang merusak koordinasi pemerintah.

Luhut sudah minta maaf kepada investor di Singapura dan memperingatkan Prabowo soal tekanan ekonomi setelah Juli 2026. 
Mahfud MD sudah bicara tentang negara gagal di forum publik.

Tapi belum ada yang berani mengambil langkah yang lebih konkret. 
Belum ada yang keluar dari koalisi. Belum ada yang memilih rakyat di atas jabatannya.

Syarat ini: belum terpenuhi. 
Ada yang mulai bergeser tapi belum ada yang berani memutus.

Dan ini yang paling membedakan 2026 dengan 1998 faktor yang bisa mempercepat ATAU memperlambat:

Yang bisa mempercepat:

Media sosial. Di 1998 informasi menyebar lewat pamflet, coretan di tembok, dan siaran radio gelap. Sekarang satu video bisa ditonton 10 juta orang dalam satu malam. 

Satu postingan bisa menggerakkan demonstrasi dalam hitungan jam. 
Pemerintah tidak bisa lagi mengontrol narasi seperti yang Soeharto lakukan.

Tekanan ekonomi global. 
Harga minyak di 117 dolar. 
Perang Iran yang Ferry Latuhihin prediksi bisa berlangsung 5 tahun. 
Tekanan eksternal yang terus menerus menggerus ruang fiskal pemerintah.

Akumulasi kekecewaan. 
Kelas menengah yang turun ke bawah tidak hanya kehilangan daya beli mereka kehilangan harapan. Dan orang yang kehilangan harapan jauh lebih mudah bergerak dibanding orang yang masih punya sesuatu untuk dipertahankan.

Yang bisa memperlambat:
Kooptasi sistematis. 
Pola yang Oki sebut demo buruh dijadikan konser, aktivis dirangkul masuk pemerintahan, kampus ditawari MBG, simbol-simbol perjuangan diambil alih menjadi simbol kekuasaan. 
Ini adalah strategi yang sangat efektif untuk memadamkan api sebelum menjadi besar.

Tidak ada figur pemersatu. 
Di 1998 ada Amien Rais, Gus Dur, Megawati tokoh-tokoh yang cukup kuat untuk mengarahkan energi rakyat. Di 2026 tidak ada satu pun figur yang bisa memainkan peran itu. 

Mahfud sudah tua dan lebih suka forum akademis. Rocky lebih suka filosofi daripada organisasi. Dan generasi muda belum menghasilkan figur yang cukup besar.

Aparat yang masih solid. 
Di 1998 ada perpecahan internal di TNI antara kelompok Wiranto dan Prabowo. 
Perpecahan itu yang membuka ruang bagi reformasi. 
Di 2026 belum ada tanda-tanda perpecahan serupa yang cukup signifikan.

Dan ini yang paling penting untuk dipahami:
Reformasi 1998 tidak terjadi karena rakyat tiba-tiba marah. Rakyat sudah marah bertahun-tahun sebelumnya. 

Tapi tidak ada yang berubah sampai tiga syarat itu terpenuhi sekaligus dalam waktu yang sangat singkat.

Yang membuat 1998 berhasil adalah pertemuan antara krisis yang tidak bisa disangkal, gerakan yang cukup terorganisir, dan elite yang memilih untuk tidak bertahan.

Di 2026 — krisisnya sedang menuju titik itu. 
Tapi belum sampai.
Gerakannya sedang dibangun. 
Tapi belum terkonsolidasi. 
Dan elite belum memilih untuk bergerak.

Tapi sejarah tidak pernah menunggu sampai semuanya siap. 
Sejarah bergerak ketika satu kejadian satu momen kritis menjadi pemicu yang menyatukan semua energi yang sudah terakumulasi.

Di 1998 — pemicunya adalah penembakan mahasiswa Trisakti.

Di 2026 — belum ada pemicu seperti itu. 
Tapi tidak ada yang bisa memastikan bahwa pemicu itu tidak akan datang.

Dan ini kalimat yang paling menghantam dari seluruh forum malam itu:

"Memilih pemimpin bodoh adalah kesalahan. 
Tapi membiarkannya terus berkuasa adalah kebodohan."

Dan Butet Kartaredjasa menutup malam itu dengan puisi yang paling menusuk:

"Jika para pemimpin tidak malu-malu merampok dengan kedok pemberian gizi dan membangun koperasi maka sesungguhnya para pemimpin sedang menyiapkan diri di gulung zaman dan mengonggok di dalam bui."

Apakah 2026 bisa menjadi Reformasi Jilid 2?

Jawaban jujurnya: belum tapi kondisinya sedang menuju ke sana.

Krisis ekonominya nyata tapi belum sampai titik 1998. Gerakannya ada tapi belum terorganisir. 
Elite-nya mulai bergeser tapi belum ada yang memutus.

Yang bisa mengubah semua itu dalam waktu sangat singkat: satu kejadian yang cukup besar untuk menjadi pemicu. 

Satu momen yang membuat semua keresahan yang sudah terakumulasi bertahun-tahun akhirnya menemukan arahnya.

Dan dalam kondisi ekonomi yang semakin buruk, hukum yang semakin menjadi sandiwara, dan komunikasi pemerintah yang semakin jauh dari kenyataan rakyat kemungkinan momen itu datang bukan semakin kecil.

Tapi perubahan yang baik tidak datang hanya dari kemarahan. Perubahan yang baik datang dari kemarahan yang diorganisir, diarahkan, dan dipimpin oleh orang-orang yang punya agenda konkret — bukan sekadar keresahan yang dikumpulkan di forum-forum kecil.

Dan itu menurut semua yang hadir malam itu di Yogyakarta adalah pekerjaan rumah terbesar yang belum selesai.

text:
Indonesia produsen sawit no 1 dunia tapi makin banyak sawit kita justru "dibakar" jadi bahan bakar, bukan diekspor atau jadi minyak goreng.

Mulai 1 Juli, kita masuk era B50. Apa itu & kenapa penting?

Apa itu B50?
Solar yang kt beli isinya bakal 50% dari sawit, 50% solar fosil. Sekarang kita di B40 (40% sawit). Naik ke B50 menjadikan Indonesia jadi negara dengan target campuran biodiesel paling agresif di dunia.

Kenapa sekarang?
Perang Iran bikin Selat Hormuz jalur ~1/5 minyak dunia ketutup. Harga minyak nembus $100/barel. Indonesia concern soal keamanan energi, jadi B50 yang tadinya ditunda, dipercepat.
Logikanya ngapain impor solar mahal kalau punya sawit sendiri?

Keuntungannya :
• Hemat tagihan impor solar ~Rp140 triliun setahun
• Buka lapangan kerja baru
• Devisa nggak lari buat beli BBM

Tapi…. Ini bagian penting juga, sawit yang dipakai buat BBM adalah sawit yang nggak jadi minyak goreng & nggak diekspor, padahal stok kita nggak nambah secepat itu. 

Artinya rebutan sawit antara tangki mobil vs dapur.

Dampak ke rakyat:
minyak goreng diprediksi naik Rp1.000–2.000/liter

Dampak ke ekspor:
Sebuah think tank (IESR) ngitung B50 bakal nahan 4–5 juta ton CPO yang harusnya diekspor setara 12–15% ekspor tahun lalu. Potensi pajak ekspor yang hilang Rp12–15 triliun setahun.
Ini angka estimasi, bukan resmi tapi ngasih gambaran skalanya.
Kapasitas juga mepet, 26 kilang biodiesel kita mampu ~22 juta kiloliter/tahun. B50 butuh ~19,5 juta. Sisa ruangnya tipis nyaris nggak ada buffer kalau ada kilang yang harus berhenti buat perawatan.

Jadi intinya ada trilema:
- Keamanan energi (kurangi impor)
- Harga pangan terjangkau
- Devisa dari ekspor

Ketiganya tarik-menarik, B50 focus yang pertama, tapi nomor 2 & 3 bayar harganya.

Indonesia lagi taruhan besar ubah komoditas ekspor andalan jadi pilar kemandirian energi. Hasilnya? Beberapa tahun ke depan baru bisa kita lihat.

(Sumber: Nikkei Asia, Bloomberg, data Kementerian ESDM)

text:
Guys, ada profesor di Beijing baru saja analisis soal kunjungan Trump ke China dan cara dia menjelaskannya menurut gue paling jujur dan paling tidak bisa dibantah dari semua analisis yang beredar.

Dan intinya satu kalimat yang langsung bikin gue terdiam:

Ini semua teater. 
Amerika dan China tidak benar-benar berperang. 
Mereka bekerja sama.

Kenapa Trump bawa 20 CEO 
senilai 12 triliun dolar dan apa artinya:

Profesor Jiang bilang sesuatu yang sangat penting dari pengalamannya di negosiasi bisnis:

kamu tidak mengumpulkan orang-orang sepenting Elon Musk, Tim Cook, Larry Fink dari BlackRock, CEO Goldman Sachs, Blackstone, Mastercard, dan Visa dalam satu ruangan kecuali ada mega deal yang mau diumumkan ke dunia.

Ini bukan kunjungan diplomatik biasa. 
Ini adalah penutupan transaksi terbesar dalam sejarah hubungan Amerika-China.

Kenapa Jensen Huang dari Nvidia tiba-tiba ikut di menit terakhir:

Ini detail yang sangat menarik. 
Sebelumnya diumumkan Jensen Huang tidak akan ikut ke Beijing. 
Tapi saat Trump transit di Alaska Jensen naik pesawat. 
Last minute.

Menurut profesor:
itu bukan kebetulan. 
Itu sinyal negosiasi. 
Scott Bessant dan timnya sedang negosiasi di Korea Selatan sebelum kunjungan ini. 

Ada jalan buntu. 
China mau chip Nvidia, 
Amerika mau akses pasar keuangan China.

Begitu ada breakthrough Jensen langsung diizinkan ikut sebagai tanda itikad baik.

Begini cara negosiasi bisnis besar bekerja. 
Bukan dengan pernyataan resmi. 
Tapi dengan sinyal siapa yang diizinkan hadir.

Apa yang masing-masing mau dan ini intinya:

China mau tiga hal: 
akses energi murah dari belahan bumi barat, 
chip Nvidia untuk AI-nya, 
dan akses pasar Amerika.

Amerika mau tiga hal juga: 
akses ke pasar keuangan China khususnya 40% tabungan rakyat China yang selama ini tidak kemana-mana kontrol atas pengembangan AI China, dan manufaktur China yang masuk ke Amerika dan Venezuela.

Soal Taiwan dan ini yang paling mengejutkan:

Profesor berani memprediksi: 
Trump kemungkinan akan mengubah posisi Amerika soal Taiwan secara dramatis. 

Dari "tidak mendukung kemerdekaan Taiwan" menjadi "mendukung reunifikasi China dan Taiwan."

Kenapa ini strategis untuk Amerika bukan hanya untuk China?

Kalau Taiwan kembali ke China masalah Taiwan tidak lagi jadi tanggung jawab Amerika. 

Masalah itu sekarang jadi tanggung jawab Jepang 
dan Korea Selatan,
karena merekalah yang paling terdampak secara geografis. 

Amerika berhasil mengalihkan beban geopolitik ke sekutunya sendiri.

Itu bukan konsesi. Itu manuver.

Teori besar yang menjelaskan segalanya mengapa China dan Amerika tidak bisa benar-benar berpisah:

Di sinilah profesor masuk ke penjelasan yang paling dalam dan paling tidak biasa.

Dia bilang: 
China adalah halusinasi dari halusinasi.

Maksudnya:
ketika Nixon ke China tahun 1972, 
itu bukan soal diplomasi atau mengimbangi Soviet. 

Alasan sesungguhnya adalah Nixon Shock 1971 ketika dolar dilepas dari standar emas dan tiba-tiba tidak bernilai apa-apa. 

Solusinya: 
ciptakan permintaan baru untuk dolar. 
Pertama lewat petrodolar minyak Timur Tengah hanya dijual dalam dolar. 

Kedua lewat China jadikan China mesin manufaktur global yang semuanya bertransaksi dalam dolar.

China tidak tumbuh karena kehebatannya sendiri. China tumbuh karena Amerika butuh tempat untuk memompa permintaan dolar. 
China adalah alat dari sistem yang diciptakan Amerika.

Dan itulah kenapa ketika China mencoba mandiri perang dagang pecah. 
Karena kalau China keluar dari sistem, 
sistem itu runtuh. 
Dan kalau sistem runtuh, 
China runtuh lebih dulu karena China adalah bagian yang paling tidak mandiri dari sistem itu.

Grand bargain yang akan terjadi dan bagaimana Indonesia relevan:

Amerika butuh China untuk membeli utangnya — senilai 39 triliun dolar dengan bunga 5% per tahun yang harus dibayar 2 triliun per tahun. 

Caranya: 
China membuka sektor keuangannya, 
rakyat China bisa beli stablecoin yang didukung obligasi Amerika, 
dan secara efektif China membiayai utang Amerika melalui konsumennya sendiri.

Dan kenapa China setuju? 
Karena pilihannya lebih buruk. 
Energi dari Timur Tengah diblokir oleh perang Iran. 

Energi dari Amerika Selatan dikontrol Trump yang baru mengumumkan Venezuela sebagai zona kepentingan Amerika. 

China butuh meja negosiasi dengan Amerika untuk memastikan pasokan energinya stabil dan terjangkau.

Ini bukan persahabatan. 
Ini adalah dua orang yang saling mencekik dan sama-sama tidak mau jatuh duluan.

Kunjungan Trump ke Beijing bukan tentang perdamaian.
Bukan tentang persahabatan.
Ini adalah dua ekonomi terbesar di dunia yang sama-sama tersandera oleh sistem yang mereka ciptakan bersama

dan sekarang mereka perlu duduk bersama untuk memastikan sistem itu tidak runtuh sebelum salah satu dari mereka siap untuk menggantinya.

Yang perlu diperhatikan Indonesia: 
kita adalah salah satu pion di papan catur ini. 
Selat Malaka ada di wilayah kita. 

Nikel dan mineral kritis kita adalah bagian dari rantai pasok yang diperebutkan keduanya. 

Dan posisi kita di antara dua superpowers ini bukan hanya soal diplomasi 

tapi soal apakah kita punya strategi yang cukup cerdas untuk tidak sekadar jadi penonton dari permainan yang hasilnya akan sangat mempengaruhi kita.

Pemerintah Arab Saudi melaporkan kepada Organisasi Negara-Negara Pengekspor Minyak (OPEC) bahwa produksi minyak mentahnya semakin anjlok pada bulan lalu, menjadi level terendah sejak 1990, karena perang Iran menghambat ekspor dari Teluk Persia.

Dikutip dari Bloomberg, kerajaan tersebut mencatat produksi minyak mentah turun lagi sebesar 651.000 barel per hari pada April 2026, menjadi 6,316 juta barel per hari, menurut laporan bulanan dari sekretariat OPEC.

Hal tersebut menambah kerugian sejak Februari menjadi 42 persen, dan menandai level terendah sejak dimulainya Perang Teluk 36 tahun yang lalu, ketika negara anggota OPEC, Irak, menyerang sesama anggota Kuwait.

Donald Trump Undang Xi Jinping Berkunjung ke AS September

Donald Trump mengundang Xi Jinping dan ibu negara Tiongkok, Peng Liyuan, untuk kunjungan balasan pada 24 September, saat ia berpidato dalam jamuan makan malam kenegaraan di Beijing pada Kamis, (14/5).

Sebelumnya, Trump disambut dengan upacara penyambutan dan keduanya mengadakan pembicaraan di Balai Agung Rakyat (Great Hall of the People), sebelum mengunjungi Kuil Surga (Temple of Heaven).

Dalam satu momen yang berkesan, jabat tangan pertama yang ikonik, Trump terlihat berusaha menarik tangan Xi ke arahnya, sebelum Xi dengan tenang menegaskan kembali otoritasnya.

Dalam pembicaraan mereka, Xi mengatakan mereka harus menjadi 'mitra, bukan rival', sementara Trump memuji Xi sebagai 'pemimpin yang hebat’.

Perjalanan Trump ke Tiongkok berlangsung pada 13-15 Mei. Ini menandai kunjungan kenegaraan keduanya ke negara tersebut dan yang pertama bagi seorang presiden AS sejak tahun 2017. Kunjungan ini sempat ditunda dari bulan April atas permintaan pihak Amerika Serikat karena perang Iran.

Xi Jinping ke Trump: Dunia Menyaksikan Pertemuan Ini, Kita Sebaiknya Jadi Mitra Bukan Rival

Presiden Xi Jinping bertemu Presiden Amerika Serikat Donald Trump dalam pembicaraan bilateral di Beijing, Kamis (14/5).

Dalam pertemuan tersebut, Xi menyerukan agar China dan Amerika Serikat menjadi mitra di tengah situasi global yang disebut semakin tidak stabil.

“China dan Amerika Serikat sama-sama akan diuntungkan dari kerja sama dan sama-sama rugi jika berkonfrontasi. Kita harus menjadi mitra, bukan rival,” kata Xi.

Ia juga menyinggung soal “Thucydides trap”, istilah yang menggambarkan kemungkinan konflik antara kekuatan lama dan kekuatan baru dunia. Xi Jinping juga menginginkan China dan Amerika mampu menciptakan hubungan baru yang lebih stabil.

Kunjungan Trump ke China berlangsung pada 13 hingga 15 Mei 2026. Bagi Trump, pertemuan ini menjadi kunjungan kenegaraan keduanya sekaligus kunjungan pertama presiden AS ke China sejak 2017. Agenda ini sebelumnya sempat ditunda dari April atas permintaan pihak Amerika Serikat akibat perang Iran.

text:
BIAYA IBADAH UMRAH NAIK

Kenaikan biaya ibadah umrah untuk musim depan tahun 1448 Hijriyah tidak dapat dielakkan. Umat muslim yang mendambakan dapat beribadah mengunjungi dua kota suci di Makkah dan Madinah akan lebih dalam merogoh koceknya.  

Beberapa hari terakhir ini sudah ada informasi pasti dari beberapa maskapai penerbangan di Indonesia terkait penyesuaian harga tiket penerbangan akibat kenaikan avtur karena kenaikan harga minyak dunia setelah perang di kawasan Teluk sejak bulan Maret 2026 lalu.

Beberapa maskapai penerbangan yang membawa jamaah umrah Indonesia; Lion Air, Batik Air Malaysia, Hainan Airlines dan Oman Air sudah menyampaikan kenaikan harga tiket grup umrah-nya masing-masing  dengan kenaikan harga mulai 1 juta rupiah hingga 5,5 juta rupiah.

Adapun Saudia Airlines, Garuda Indonesia, Ethiopian Airlines, Qatar Airways, Etihad Airways, Emirates Airlines, Indigo, Scoot dan Air Asia sudah menampilkan penyesuaian harga terbaru tanpa menggunakan surat resmi namun langsung menyampaikan harga terbarunya, yang tentunya mengalami kenaikan harga juga.

Mau tidak mau bagi pelaku usaha industri ibadah Umrah (PPIU) kenaikan harga paket umrah mulai musim mendatang sekitar pertengahan Juni 2026 akan mengalami kenaikan harga.

Bagi penulis, yang mungkin dapat disarankan terkait kondisi global yang berhubungan dengan geopolitik di Timur Tengah dan kawasan Teluk yang masih tetap "panas" bagi calon jamaah umrah Indonesia dalam pemilihan maskapai penerbangan adalah; selain tentunya pilihan terkait dengan harga dan juga hal yang penting adalah rute penerbangan. 

Pada awal terjadinya perang Iran vs Israel (Amerika Serikat) maskapai penerbangan yang tetap mendapatkan prioritas untuk tetap terbang adalah yang direct flight atau penerbangan langsung dengan rute Jakarta-Jeddah. Rute ini dimiliki oleh maskapai Saudia Airlines, Garuda Indonesia dan Lion Air. 

Saran selanjutnya dengan panasnya kondisi geopolitik ini adalah maskapai penerbangan yang rute penerbangannya menjauh dari kawasan Teluk, seperti contohnya Ethiopian Airlines yang transit di home base-nya kota Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, baru kemudian menuju kota Jeddah. Rute ini secara otomatis secara geografis menjauh dari kawasan Teluk.

Semoga kondisi geopolitik dunia segera makin membaik agar perjalanan ibadah umrah dan haji khususnya dari Indonesia dapat kembali berjalan lancar dan aman.

7. Asian Energy, Maritime, and Economic Enforcement Compact

China, India, Japan, South Korea, Pakistan, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and other participating Asian states shall be invited to join the settlement as energy purchasers, maritime-security partners, diplomatic guarantors, reconstruction contributors, and economic-enforcement partners.

Participation shall require concrete commitments rather than statements of concern alone.

A. China

China shall be requested to:

Use its commercial influence with Iran to secure uninterrupted civilian passage through the Strait of Hormuz.
Join the international monitoring commission and serve as a guarantor of Iran’s compliance with the navigation agreement.
Condition new Iranian energy investments and financing upon continued compliance.
Purchase additional lawful Gulf exports and help stabilize energy prices during the transition.
Prevent Chinese ports, banks, shipping companies, and intermediaries from circumventing measures adopted against designated Israeli or Iranian military entities.
Suspend military-capable components, surveillance technology, drones, artificial-intelligence systems, and dual-use exports to any designated entity attempting to sabotage the settlement.
Support a binding Security Council resolution establishing the ceasefire, monitoring system, Palestinian political process, and maritime mission.

China would not be required to join a Western military coalition. Its responsibility would be to use the economic leverage created by its relationship with Iran and its position as a major energy purchaser.

B. India

India shall be requested to:

Participate in the monitoring and protection of civilian commercial shipping.
Provide naval rescue, escort, medical, and mine-countermeasure capabilities under a defensive mandate.
Use its relationships with Israel, Iran, the Gulf states, and the United States to serve as an independent diplomatic channel.
Apply enhanced end-use monitoring to prevent Indian technology, software, components, or financial services from supporting prohibited military operations.
Suspend new contracts with designated Israeli military entities while maintaining essential civilian commerce.
Contribute engineering, medical, communications, and infrastructure support to Palestinian reconstruction.

India’s balanced relationships make it especially suitable as an intermediary that cannot easily be characterized as belonging exclusively to either camp.

C. Japan and South Korea

Japan and South Korea shall be requested to:

Convert their support for secure navigation into participation in a strictly defensive maritime mission.
Provide mine-clearance vessels, surveillance for civilian navigation, rescue capacity, port logistics, and emergency tanker assistance.
Establish strategic purchasing agreements for redirected Azerbaijani, Kazakh, Nigerian, Gulf, and other lawful oil supplies.
Suspend exports of military-capable electronics, semiconductors, optical equipment, machine tools, artificial-intelligence systems, and dual-use components to designated entities.
Restrict financing, insurance, maintenance, and technological support for prohibited Israeli or Iranian military operations.
Finance desalination, electricity, hospitals, telecommunications, housing, and transportation infrastructure in a future Palestinian state.

D. Pakistan and Muslim-majority Asian states

Pakistan, Indonesia, Malaysia, Bangladesh, and other participating Muslim-majority Asian states shall:

Support Saudi, Turkish, Qatari, and Omani mediation with Iran.
Participate in Palestinian reconstruction and diplomatic recognition efforts.
Coordinate lawful targeted sanctions against persons and entities responsible for grave violations.
Prevent fundraising, weapons transfers, or recruitment intended to undermine the settlement.
Support a two-state outcome while expressly protecting Israeli and Palestinian civilians.

Pakistan may contribute maritime and diplomatic capacity, but any military participation must remain defensive, internationally authorized, and subordinate to the ceasefire.

E. Singapore and Asian commercial centers

Singapore and other major Asian financial and maritime centers shall:

Enforce beneficial-ownership disclosure for cargo, vessels, insurers, brokers, and purchasing companies.
Deny port, banking, insurance, and brokerage services to designated sanctions evaders.
Inspect suspicious transshipment arrangements intended to conceal the destination of oil, weapons, or dual-use technology.
Establish penalties for falsified end-user certificates, ship-to-ship sanctions evasion, and concealed military procurement.
Protect legitimate civilian trade from unnecessary interruption.

F. Asian purchaser coalition

Participating Asian and European states shall establish an Energy Redirection Facility to purchase oil voluntarily redirected away from prohibited Israeli military or state-controlled purchasers.

The facility shall:

Guarantee alternative buyers for participating exporters.
Use transparent market pricing rather than confiscation.
Track cargo ownership and final destinations.
Prohibit resale to designated entities.
Protect civilian energy supplies necessary for hospitals, water, emergency transportation, and other essential services.
Release participating suppliers from restrictions once compliance benchmarks are independently verified.

G. Asian measures concerning Israel

Asian participants shall adopt graduated measures against the Israeli government and designated entities when independently verified violations occur. These may include:

Suspension of offensive military exports and dual-use technology.
Restrictions on military-linked investment, financing, insurance, shipping, and procurement.
Suspension of government-sponsored research and technology partnerships involving designated entities.
Exclusion of settlement goods.
Asset freezes and travel restrictions against responsible officials, commanders, violent settlers, organizations, and commercial facilitators.
Recognition of Palestine and support for its full participation in international institutions.
Coordinated diplomatic action demanding a ceasefire, humanitarian access, an end to settlement expansion, and time-bound negotiations toward two sovereign states.

No measure shall intentionally deprive Israeli civilians of food, medicine, water, civilian electricity, emergency communications, or other essential necessities.

H. Performance requirement

Every participating Asian state shall file a public implementation report every thirty days identifying:

Shipping protected or cleared for passage.
Energy purchased through the redirection mechanism.
Restricted military and dual-use exports.
Sanctions-evasion attempts detected.
Humanitarian and reconstruction funding delivered.
Diplomatic or verification commitments completed.

A state issuing supportive statements without implementing its pledged measures shall not be represented as a guarantor of the agreement.

8. Trump’s Asian burden-sharing formulation

President Trump may describe the arrangement as follows:

For years, the countries most dependent on Middle Eastern energy issued statements while America carried the military and financial burden. Under this agreement, Asia will help secure the shipping lanes, purchase redirected energy, prevent sanctions evasion, finance reconstruction, and enforce the peace. China will use its leverage with Iran. India will help bridge the parties. Japan and South Korea will protect commercial navigation. Every major beneficiary of an open Strait will contribute to keeping it open.

This approach gives Asian states a choice: participate materially in regional stability or lose the diplomatic prestige associated with claiming to support peace.

Let's address this nonsense about Trump "ending" wars.

INDIA AND PAKISTAN:

This was not a "war," but a military escalation after a terrorist attack in Kashmir earlier last year.

Both countries negotiated an end to the fighting directly with one another. Trump claims to have mediated it, but there are conflicting accounts.

India did not directly credit Trump with ending the fighting, Modi insisted this wasn't the case and it's no coincidence that India reckoned with a massive 50 percent tariff from Trump in response.

Pakistan, however, said it would nominate Trump for a Nobel Peace Prize and faced a much lower tariff rate.

Any chance of a permanent peace between the two countries is nil while Trump's alleged mediation did nothing to address the underlying causes of the conflict. This was a political stunt.

While the Trump administration claims that India's excessively high tariff rate had to do with them buying Russian oil, it wasn't imposed for this reason. In fact, the rate was originally intended to be lower until India refused to acknowledge that Trump was chiefly involved in mediating the conflict.

And it's certainly not hard to believe considering that Trump has been basing his tariff policies off of whether countries "come to the table" with offers that benefit him personally, politically or financially.

AZERBAIJAN AND ARMENIA:

Trump claims to have negotiated a peace deal between Azerbaijan and Armenia.

This was evidently not a "peace deal," but a photo op. Leaders shook hands in front of cameras at the White House, half heartedly agreeing to a "commitment" to peace that neither side has since shown interest in. Diplomatic ties still remain broken, barriers still remain in place and both sides continue to quarrel with each other over borders and territory.

Part of the agreement however, included that Armenia grant the US the right to build "the Trump Route for Peace and Prosperity," a transit corridor through Armenia and a project that Trump is no doubt meant to personally benefit from.

There's no indication of when this "route" will start developing or on what terms.

RWANDA AND THE CONGO:

Once again, leaders and diplomats from both countries came to the White House to publicly sign an agreement that aimed to carve out a path for a future peace. Trump took responsibility for it and barely credited Qatar for the major role it played in brokering the deal. 

However, peace talks between the two countries have since failed and many have died as violent and deadly fighting escalate in the region. Rwandan backed forces almost immediately threatened to withdraw from the agreement while both sides of this conflict have violated its terms. In other words, there is no agreement.

But what does Trump care? He already got his publicity stunt out of it.

CAMBODIA AND THAILAND:

Both were engaged in days of fighting when Trump levied economic threats against the two neighbors unless they agreed to a ceasefire.

Malaysia got primarily involved and organized talks days later that included some American officials. The countries reached a temporary deal that paused hostilities under Malaysia's supervision. Trump took credit of course and added this to his "wars that I ended" list. 

Trump's supposed intervention did nothing to address the root causes of the conflict. Both countries continued quarreling over claims to Hindu Temples along their respective borders.

EGYPT AND ETHIOPIA:

This one wasn't even a military conflict, but a diplomatic feud over a hydroelectric dam that Ethiopia built.

Trump did nothing to resolve the dispute, and both Egypt and Sudan fervently oppose the project, claiming it will restrict the flow of water into their countries.

Yet Trump has used this as another shining example of his unrivaled ability to "end wars."

SERBIA AND KOSOVO:

The last war between these two countries ended in 1999. This one's not even worth addressing.

Sept. 16—The 18th annual BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, which convened Sept. 12-13, took to a higher level the existing process of collaboration among nations of the Global South toward a new world order for economic development and security. Running under the banner, “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability,” the summit can be seen as an international capstone to the earlier Eurasian-centered multi-nation conferences earlier this month, conducted with the same spirit of dialogue for mutual benefit: the Shanghai Cooperation Organization in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan (Aug. 31-Sept. 1), and the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok, Russia (Sept. 1-4). There are grounds to expect expression of this new, positive leadership dynamic in certain speeches to the UN General Assembly in its upcoming, annual General Debate, Sept. 22-28, titled, “Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations that Delivers for All.”

As Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the host of this year’s summit, emphasized, the 21 BRICS member and partner countries represent more than 50% of the world’s population, 40% of global GDP, and more than 25% of global trade—truly a grouping that is already playing a major global role today. The New Delhi proceedings included the BRICS Business Forum on Sept. 11—reportedly the biggest gathering yet of business leaders from the BRICS nations—the 11-member summit on Sept. 12, and the full 21-member BRICS-Plus the next day. A joint “New Delhi Declaration” was released, 45 pages in length, with 140 points.

‘Partners Not Rivals’

Prime Minister Narendra Modi, host of the summit, used the expression of nations being “partners not rivals,” which characterizes the diplomatic, economic, and social interactions throughout the proceedings of the historic BRICS weekend. Modi spoke those words specifically in reference to relations between China and India, in his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping Sept. 12. Nonetheless, the concept portends an overall shift away from the dying and dangerous Western geopolitical model, into a new world model in which the common interests of nations are advanced, and problems resolved.
(Front row:) Russian President Vladimir Putin (left) and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the 18th BRICS Summit.
(Front row:) Russian President Vladimir Putin (left) and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the 18th BRICS Summit. Credit: https://t.co/cRRPijvBAL

This success of the BRICS event confounded the attempts by Western geopolitical circles to cause splits and dissension wherever they could. Western media focused on imputed “limits” to any China-India “thaw” and on BRICS as merely a talk-shop that will never be able to reach any substantive agreements. But the event proved these predictions wrong. Despite the United States’ Operation Economic Outcast, which unilaterally decrees sanctions and economic warfare against Iran and any nation having commercial dealings with it, Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian participated fully in the summit, including meeting with Prime Minister Modi and many others on the sidelines. Economic agreements were made between Iran and India, and with the Eurasian Economic Union. The U.S.’ delusional “Economic Outcast” decree was ignored.
President of China Xi Jinping during the 18th BRICS Summit.
President of China Xi Jinping during the 18th BRICS Summit. Credit: https://t.co/cRRPijvBAL

Notably, the representative of Cuba, another government the U.S. President Donald Trump Administration has labeled a pariah state to be razed to the ground, received the same warm welcome that the Indian hosts extended to all.

In another indication, the final joint Declaration unanimously denounced the policy of sanctions and the illegal operations against Ibero-America, in a clear gesture toward the United States. Instead of splintering, the group is exhibiting a growing unity.

“BRICS has come of age,” declared Prime Minister Modi, who was quoted by senior Indian diplomat M.K. Bhadrakumar, former Indian ambassador to Russia and other nations. Bhadrakumar concurred, pointing out many key aspects of the summit, especially that Chinese President Xi Jinping called on BRICS to become more involved in “peacekeeping.”

Three heads of state and one head of government of the core five founding BRICS member nations participated in New Delhi: Host Prime Minister Modi, President Xi, Russian President Vladimir Putin, who spent three days in India, and South African President Cyril Ramaphosa. Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sent Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira in his stead, because the Brazilian national election will occur Oct. 4, in which Lula himself is a presidential candidate.

Of the other six newer BRICS member nations, heads of state or government attended from Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the United Arab Emirates, and Indonesia, and the Foreign Minister from Saudi Arabia. The 10 BRICS Partner Nations (Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan, Nigeria, and Vietnam) were represented by either their head of state or other high official, as were a number of invited guest nations. In addition, country chairs of developing-nation groupings were invited, including the African Union, ASEAN, CELAC in the Americas, and the Gulf Cooperation Council.

A total of 2,000 delegates went to New Delhi, with many hundreds of others also in attendance. High officials from the United Nations and other associations came, including UN Secretary General António Guterres and World Health Organization Director General Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus.
Development—The ‘Biggest Common Denominator’

The positive diplomacy that characterized the dozens of bilateral and multi-nation meetings over the summit weekend was not a façade, nor did it paper over the significant differences and frictions that exist between nations. The goodwill came from the explicitly stated goals of respecting diversity, seeking to resolve conflicts peaceably through negotiation, and sharing the goal of serving a common good. There were two outstanding examples in this domain, as well as many less dramatic examples: The leaders of India and China met, and the leaders of Iran and the United Arab Emirates met.
Indian and Chinese Leaders Met

The long-standing friction between India and China is well known, including border disputes and India’s large trade deficit with China, which in 2025 hit $120 billion. President Xi had not been to India since 2019. But on Sept. 12, Modi and Xi held a productive, 50-minute meeting.

On Sept. 14, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun gave a lengthy reply to a reporter, indicating the importance China gives to the meeting between the two leaders. “The meeting in New Delhi marks the two leaders’ ‘reaffirmation’ of the growth of China-India ties after guiding the bilateral relations from starting afresh in Kazan to making further improvements in Tianjin. The most important consensus reached is that China and India should be partners,” Guo said.

“As President Xi noted, China and India have different national realities. We should draw on each other’s strengths, support each other, help each other succeed, and develop together,” he continued. He quoted Modi as saying that “India has an independent foreign policy, developing relations with China is not affected by any third party and it will not allow any force to engage in anti-China activities on its territory.” China values Prime Minister Modi’s statements, Guo said.

“The two leaders agreed that as the most populous countries in the world and major members of the Global South, China and India should focus on development, which is the biggest common denominator,” he went on. “The two sides should also address each other’s economic and trade concerns in a balanced way and promote the sound and steady development of economic and trade relations. The two sides agreed to support each other in chairing BRICS, promote cooperation in the Global South, help build a multipolar world, and serve as forces for progress and stability in the volatile world. At the same time, the two leaders agree to properly handle the disputes and disagreements between China and India to jointly safeguard peace and tranquility in the border area.” China will host the BRICS Summit 2027.

The two nations have already set follow-up into motion. Indian Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal reported that on Sept. 12 Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao and Indian Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal had met in New Delhi to begin to flesh out each other’s positions on various trade-related problems. He stated, “Leaders have already guided that both sides should work together to address each other’s concerns, and also try to look at structural trade imbalance, supply-chain issues, and how to build trust between the two sides…. This was the initial meeting; there will be more meetings subsequently to take these discussions forward.”
Iranian and UAE Leaders Met

Also on Sept. 12, Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian met with the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, who is in line to be the next President of the United Arab Emirates. Both Iran and the UAE signed the joint Declaration calling for restraint over escalating tensions in the Middle East. For these two countries, divided by war, this can be seen as a sign of diplomatic progress. The UAE broke off diplomatic relations with Iran on March 1 this year. Iran has targeted U.S. military bases in the UAE, which in turn has joined the United States and Israel in strikes on Iran.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addresses the BRICS Summit.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addresses the BRICS Summit. Credit: CC/MEAphotogallery

The wording in the Declaration’s text includes: “We express deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in Middle East/West Asia … call for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation.”

The Declaration’s paragraph on nuclear safety, implying strongly that there must be no military attacks on nuclear plants, is of special significance: “The growing risks of nuclear danger and conflict are a cause of deep concern. Nuclear safeguards, safety, and security must always be upheld, including in armed conflicts.”

In the Iranian read-out of the meeting between Pezeshkian and the crown prince, Tehran reported that Pezeshkian, “stressed Iran’s principled approach of using dialogue to resolve disputes and warned against efforts by adversaries to create division among Muslim countries…. He stressed that Iran had not started the war and had targeted U.S. bases only in self-defense, including facilities used to launch attacks against Iran, which martyred the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, as well as commanders, scientists and children…. President Pezeshkian said regional security could not be achieved through U.S. military presence, emphasizing that countries in the region should discuss and decide on their own security independently.”
Modi: Win-Win in Diversity

Prime Minister Modi, as the summit’s host, delivered opening remarks on Sept. 12 which emphasized that the BRICS’s strength lies precisely in its diversity and its ability to bring development to all parties. Throughout the summit, Modi had multiple bilateral meetings, notably with Iran’s President, and also conferred with BRICS co-founder leaders, with whom he had just recently met in Bishkek.

Modi began his keynote by stating, “I am pleased that, with all your cooperation and support, we have been able to translate our shared vision into win-win cooperation.” It will not have gone unnoticed that he used the phrase “win-win,” which is widely associated with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Modi added, “From my personal experience, I can say that the Global South countries’ confidence in BRICS has grown, because within BRICS: Their voices are heard. Their experiences are respected. And solutions are developed not for them, but together with them.”

Modi’s conclusion was particularly eloquent: “The strength of BRICS lies in our diversity and cooperation. We may be rooted in different realities, but together, we rise through cooperation, and blossom for humanity. May our diversity remain our identity, our cooperation become our inspiration, and our progress serve the cause of all humanity.”

The meeting on the summit’s sidelines between Modi and Xi, also centered on the agreement of the two leaders that their countries “are partners rather than rivals.” India’s Ministry of External Affairs issued a statement reporting on that historic conversation, which said: “They reaffirmed that both countries should take a strategic and long-term perspective of their ties. Differences should not become disputes. The Prime Minister [Modi] highlighted that both sides must be guided by three mutuals—mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest.”

The statement continued: “He [Modi] underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues. The two leaders expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question proceeding from the political perspective of their overall bilateral relations and the long-term interests of the two peoples.”
Putin: Establish a ‘Common Growth Platform’

It is regarded as unusual that President Putin spent three whole days on a foreign trip, which he did in New Delhi with a packed agenda of bilateral meetings, and summit sessions, on wide-ranging topics. On Sept. 13, he addressed the BRICS-Plus assembly, noting, “The BRICS group has always advocated that all countries without exception should have equal and unlimited opportunities for consistent and balanced economic and social growth, for ensuring their populations’ wellbeing, while being able to preserve unique national cultures and traditions and to adhere to their own sovereign development models,” according to the Kremlin site.

In his remarks, Putin also returned to a theme at the center of his earlier interventions at the BRICS Business Forum, and his speech to the plenary session: to convert the BRICS and its institutions, such as the New Development Bank, into the motor for high-tech development for the entire Global South. “The potential for the further development of BRICS is far from exhausted. One of the main untapped resources so far is the complementarity of the member states’ economies…. In essence, the goal is to establish a common growth platform for BRICS that would organically integrate the competitive advantages of our economies.”

Putin continued: “I must emphasize that it is crucial to build this platform on the principles of openness and accessibility, not only for BRICS members, but for all our partners and friends. I am confident that this is precisely what will happen.” He then emphasized a Russian initiative that is being considered, but has not yet been adopted by the BRICS:

“I also invite everyone to take a closer look at the promising initiatives put forward by Russia to streamline our cooperation. These include establishing a BRICS payment, depository and clearance infrastructure, as well as setting up a reinsurance mechanism and a grain exchange within the association…. Further strengthening the capacity of the BRICS New Development Bank and updating its business model is a pressing task…. A new investment platform could help meet these demands. By leveraging modern financial technologies—including digital assets—such a platform would make it possible to mobilize long-term capital, including private funds, not only for the BRICS nations but also, crucially, for the economies of our partners across the Global South and East.”
New Development Bank (BRICS Bank) headquarters in Shanghai, China.
New Development Bank (BRICS Bank) headquarters in Shanghai, China. Credit: CC/Donnie28

President Putin met in New Delhi Sept. 11 with New Development Bank (NDB) President Dilma Rousseff, former President of Brazil, where the two discussed ways of advancing the bank beyond the bounds of the Western financial system. The NDB is still somewhat tethered to the U.S. dollar system. So following the imposition of Western sanctions against Russia, the bank was forced to freeze project financing for Russia or risk being denied access to Anglo-American-dominated capital markets. As a result, none of the 123 projects the NDB had approved for construction in Russia or involving its firms, worth nearly U.S. $40 billion, were implemented. But that is expected to change.

Rousseff told Putin: “I am very optimistic about the future, as we have taken steps to address the difficulties and the profound injustice the Russian Federation faced on the part of the Bank. After all, the Russian Federation has always played a pivotal role and acted with integrity towards the Bank.” Rousseff concluded: “Unfortunately, for various reasons, things unfolded as they did. Yet now, it seems to me, we have found the right path to putting this injustice right.”
Xi Jinping: ‘A New Chapter of Strength through Unity’

China’s President Xi Jinping used his two addresses to the BRICS Summit—the first to the plenary of members on Sept. 12; the second to the expanded BRICS-Plus gathering on Sept. 13—to both evaluate the progress made by the BRICS in its first 20 years of existence, and to make a series of concrete proposals for the grouping’s direction now. This gives insight into what is expected from China’s assumption of the BRICS rotating presidency in 2027.

In his first address, Xi emphasized the BRICS’s pioneering role. “Standing at the forefront of the Global South, we BRICS countries have upheld independence, actively explored development paths suited to our respective national conditions, and set a fine example of emerging markets and developing countries seeking strength through unity.” He noted that the world today is gravely lacking peace and development, and added: “For the exact purpose of addressing these deficits and building a better world, I have put forward the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative, the Global Civilization Initiative and the Global Governance Initiative … [to] work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity.”

Xi then presented what the Chinese media has called his “four pioneers”: “First, BRICS should be a pioneer in advancing innovation-driven development…. Second, BRICS should be a pioneer in upholding peace and stability…. We should act on the vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security.” He specifically mentioned the crisis in Southwest Asia: “The situation in the Middle East remains complex and fluid…. The relevant parties should keep to the direction of political settlement, and work for a permanent, comprehensive ceasefire. Attention should be paid to addressing the problems at the source, rebuilding trust between regional countries, and establishing a new security architecture. The Palestinian question is always at the core of the Middle East issue, and the fundamental way forward is to implement the two-state solution and realize peaceful coexistence between Palestine and Israel….

“Third, BRICS should be a pioneer in facilitating mutual learning between civilizations…. BRICS should be a garden of inclusive coexistence that allows various civilizations to flourish. We should promote the common values of humanity, and advocate exchange, mutual learning and harmonious coexistence between civilizations….

“Fourth, BRICS should be a pioneer in reforming and improving global governance.”

Xi concluded his first speech by emphasizing, “Together, we will usher in the third golden decade of BRICS cooperation, and open up a bright prospect of shared prosperity and progress.”

In his second speech, delivered on Sept. 13 to the BRICS-Plus gathering, President Xi began, “We meet at a time when changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world…. The international landscape is volatile and fraught with risks and challenges. To bring stability to the world and make it a better place, BRICS countries must seize the historical initiative, rally the Global South, be an active, stabilizing and positive force in international affairs, and advance the well-being of all humanity.”

He continued: “The logic of ‘might makes right’ does not hold, and should have been discarded long ago. Global South countries should jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, safeguard the basic norms of international relations including sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs, and the peaceful settlement of disputes.”

Like President Putin, Xi emphasized, “We should support the operation and development of the New Development Bank to facilitate Global South cooperation. The international financial architecture must be reformed and improved to increase the representation and voice of developing countries.”

He then proceeded to enumerate his five initiatives:

“First, the open source and inclusive AI initiative…. Second, the trade and investment facilitation initiative…. Third, the digital industry cooperation initiative…. Fourth, the intelligent manufacturing cooperation initiative…. Fifth, the science and technology talent development initiative.”

He concluded by stating that China will continue to “promote high-quality Belt and Road cooperation to share opportunities and prosper together with all countries. Let us work as one to promote greater BRICS cooperation and write a new chapter of strength through unity for the Global South!”

Dennis Small, Gretchen Small and Stewart Battle contributed to this article.
